description: Four waveform outputs whose position in the cycle is set by a voltage you patch in, rather than by an oscillator of its own

params.text: Chooses the span the phase input is read over: -5V to 5V in the B position, 0V to 10V in the U position
Chooses what happens to a phase voltage outside that span: Clamp holds it at the end of the cycle, Wrap carries it round to the start again
Chooses whether the outputs run from 0V upwards in the U position or centred on 0V in the B position
Sets how wide the output span is, from 0V for a flat output to 10V at the far right
Attenuates and inverts the Range input between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Sets the pulse width, from 1% counter-clockwise to 99% clockwise, at half width in the centre
Attenuates and inverts the PWM input between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Shapes the waveforms, sharpening their peaks counter-clockwise and rounding them clockwise; the square instead morphs into a triangle counter-clockwise and into a saw clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the MOD input between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%

inputs.text: Sets where in the cycle each output is, over the 10V span picked by the switch beside it; a polyphonic signal here gives every output the same number of channels
Adds its voltage to the span set by the Range knob, a volt of input widening the span by a volt once the trim knob is up
Moves the pulse width, 5V covering half the knob's travel once the trim knob is up
Moves the shaping, 10V covering the knob's full travel once the trim knob is up

outputs.text: The square, high over the part of the phase span set by the pulse width
The triangle, at the top of its range a quarter of the way through the phase span
The falling saw, at the top of its range where the phase input is at the bottom of its span
The sine, one full cycle over the phase span

notes: nothing comes out until a voltage is patched into the phase input; with the jack empty every output holds at one fixed point of the cycle
this is the one LFO here with no rate of its own, so there is no frequency knob, no sync and no rate chaos; the outputs go as fast as the phase voltage moves, audio rate included
menu: Pulse-width mode: All waveforms, Square only — chooses whether the pulse-width control warps the phase of every waveform or only sets the width of the square
Pulse-width range: 1% to 99%, 5% to 95%, 10% to 90%, 15% to 85%, 20% to 80%, 25% to 75% — narrows what the pulse-width knob covers end to end
Invert (all) waveforms — flips all four waveforms within the range, and lights a small red mark above the output jacks
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed

inputs.1:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.2:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.

±5V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
